roadmap.goal: A Jira or a Linear instance gets everything slices 01 and 02 delivered from its own tracker's links, with nothing re-entered by hand. Jira reads the inward half of issuelinks off the response the fetch already returns; Linear reads a Project's inverse relations off the projects query it already sends. Neither tracker gains a request. ServiceNow and CSV keep yielding nothing and complaining about nothing. Everything downstream of the connector - reconcile, verdict, warnings, route - is untouched, and the earlier slices' scenarios are re-run over each connector's real mapper rather than copied per connector.

phases.name: Jira reads the half of a link that means waiting

steps.name: The inward half of issuelinks, as references
steps.scenario_name: A Jira Feature's inward links become dependencies, and its outward ones do not
criteria: A link whose type.inward reads "is blocked by" and which carries an inwardIssue yields that issue's key.
A link carrying only an outwardIssue yields nothing, whichever way its type is named.
An issue with no issuelinks field, an empty one, or entries missing type or key yields nothing and throws nothing.
The reference is the key verbatim - no trimming, no case change - because that is what ReferenceId holds.
Nothing reads the link's display name for anything a user sees.
steps.implementation_notes:
Issue.Fields already holds the raw fields element, so this is a pure function over JsonElement and needs no change to IssueFactory and no change to any request. The Cloud fixture in IssueFactoryTest already carries "issuelinks":[] , which is the evidence that *all returns it; Data Center sends no fields= at all and gets Jira's navigable default, which includes it too.

RED MECHANISM: statically-typed trunk-green repo. A test naming an absent member does not compile, so the run would be BROKEN rather than RED. Author the test [Ignore("pending - DELIVER (epic-4365)")] beside a minimal skeleton and un-ignore one at a time; main must always compile.

steps.name: A Jira Feature carries what it waits on, and nothing else moves
steps.scenario_name: Reading Jira's link information changes nothing else Lighthouse already read
criteria: A Feature built from a Jira issue carries one dependency reference per inward blocking link.
Every other mapped value on that Feature is byte-identical to what the same fixture produced before this step.
The Cloud search request still asks for *all and the Data Center one still names no fields at all.
The identity sweep still asks for key,updated and nothing more, on both flavours.
The refresh makes no request it did not make before.
steps.implementation_notes:
The one edit that could do real damage in this slice is widening SweepFields. Do not touch it. It is the change-detection pass, it never maps a field, and keeping it at key,updated is the whole reason a Data Center portfolio refresh went from 468856 ms to 2087 ms in Epic #5687. The DESIGN wave named the sweep's line as the place to edit; that was wrong.

The edit is one argument at the new Feature(...) call in CreateFeaturesFromIssues, mirroring what the ADO connector already does.

steps.name: A renamed link type says so instead of failing quietly
steps.scenario_name: A Jira instance that has renamed its link type says so instead of failing quietly
criteria: When a Portfolio's issues carry inward links but none match, one warning names the Portfolio and the distinct inward names that were seen.
When some link did match, nothing is logged - a working instance is not warned at.
When no issue carried any link at all, nothing is logged - having no dependencies is not a misconfiguration.
One line per refresh, never one per issue or one per link.
The names are read from the tracker and reach only the log; nothing a user sees gains a Jira word.
steps.implementation_notes:
This is the answer to the slice's learning hypothesis, and it keeps the answer inside the mapper rather than growing a second configuration surface beside slice 04's field pointer. Aggregated, one line, consistent with slice 02's log-noise decision (one WARN per loop, one aggregated line for unforecastable blockers).

IDependencyRefreshReporter is the wrong home: it reports on a Portfolio's reconciled Features, and this is a fact about a payload, known before any Feature exists.

phases.name: Linear reads the far side of the relation

steps.name: A Project's inverse relations, as references
steps.scenario_name: A Linear Feature's dependencies resolve even though the tracker names them differently
criteria: The projects query asks for inverseRelations beside the fields it already asks for, in the same request.
Each inverse relation yields its source project's id, stored verbatim as the reference.
A Project with no inverse relations, a null connection or a node missing its project yields nothing and throws nothing.
The reference resolves against a Feature whose ReferenceId is that same project id.
No second request is sent for relations.
steps.implementation_notes:
Settled against linear/linear's published schema.graphql on 2026-08-21, recorded in the delta. A ProjectRelation has project (the source), relatedProject (the target) and type. A Project's inverseRelations are the ones where it is the target - what it is waiting on. Its own relations are what it blocks, and D14 excludes that direction on every connector.

The DESIGN's "dependencies connection" does not exist on Project; it is an Issue field, and a Lighthouse Feature is a Linear Project. There is no lower-case fold on this path: CreateFeatureFromProject keys a Feature by projectNode.Id, the raw id, and the relation returns the other end in the same form.

Test pattern is the one LinearWorkTrackingConnectorHistoryParsingTest already uses: a faked HttpMessageHandler returning a canned GraphQL body, no live workspace.

steps.name: The near side of the relation contributes nothing
criteria: A Project that blocks another carries no dependency of its own from that fact.
The query does not request relations, so the near side cannot be read by accident later.
A fixture carrying both directions produces exactly one edge, pointing from the blocked Project to the blocking one.
Every other mapped value on a Linear Feature is unchanged by this phase.
steps.implementation_notes: Reading the near side would produce a count that looks right on every screen while pointing every edge the wrong way, which is worse than reading nothing. The both-directions fixture is what makes the assertion mean something: one relation, two Projects, exactly one edge.

phases.name: The trackers with nothing to read, and the one already working

steps.name: No dependency field is not an error
steps.scenario_name: A tracker with no dependency link yields nothing and complains about nothing
criteria: A CSV Feature is waiting on nothing, carries no dependency warning and produces no log line about dependencies.
ServiceNow's refusal to return Features at all is unchanged and unmentioned by anything in this epic.
No connector gains a member it has nothing to implement.
steps.implementation_notes: Expected to be assertion-only: CSV builds its Features through the single-argument constructor, which leaves the list empty, and ServiceNow throws NotSupportedException from GetFeaturesForProject so no Feature exists for an edge to be between. If either needs a production edit, that is the signal the port grew a per-connector obligation it should not have.

steps.name: Azure DevOps is unchanged by the two beside it
steps.scenario_name: Azure DevOps behaviour is unchanged by the two trackers added beside it
criteria: Every existing Azure DevOps dependency test passes untouched.
An ADO Feature built from the slice-01 fixture carries exactly the edges it carried after slice 01.
No file under the AzureDevOps connector directory is modified by this slice.
steps.implementation_notes: Guarded by the diff as much as by the suite: if this slice touches the ADO connector, the claim is already false. Verify with git diff --stat before calling the step done.

steps.name: The earlier slices' scenarios, re-run through each connector's real mapper
steps.scenario_name: Everything the earlier slices delivered behaves the same on every tracker
criteria: One scenario body runs over three connectors; there is no per-connector copy of it.
The Jira and Linear cases build their Features through the real mapper from a tracker payload, not by hand.
The row's count, the named entries and the outside-this-Portfolio warning read identically on all three.
Adding a fourth connector to the list requires no change to the scenario body.
If the parameterisation is awkward, that is recorded as the learning hypothesis failing rather than worked around.
steps.implementation_notes:
The existing acceptance harness fakes IWorkTrackingConnector, which is exactly the seam that makes everything downstream connector-agnostic by construction. Parameterising means varying how the faked port's Feature list is produced: hand-built for ADO, and through the real Jira and Linear mappers from a payload fixture for the other two. That is what turns a structural claim into a tested one.

This is the step that answers AC-9.5 and it is the one to write last, because it is also the readback on whether phases 01 and 02 put the mapping in the right place.

steps.name: Neither tracker is asked for anything more
steps.scenario_name: Reading dependencies costs each tracker's refresh nothing extra to speak of
criteria: A Jira portfolio refresh sends the same number of requests, to the same URLs, as it did before this slice.
A Linear portfolio refresh sends the same number of requests, and the projects query grows only by the fields it selects.
The assertion counts requests rather than timing them, because a wall clock in a unit test measures the machine.
The wall-clock half of AC-9.6 is recorded as owed against the dogfood instance, not faked here.
steps.implementation_notes:
The precedent is AzureDevOpsDependencyRelationTest's GetFeaturesForProject_ReadingTheDependenciesCostsTheRefreshNoRequestOfItsOwn. Same shape, same claim, one per tracker.

AC-9.6's 110% clause needs a real instance and a real payload; it belongs to the manual verification the maintainer is doing at the end of the epic, and the slice verdict must say so rather than implying a number was measured.

walking_skeleton: Slice 01 shipped the walking skeleton against real Azure DevOps data. This slice adds no new path through the system, only two more sources feeding the one it already has, so it re-runs that skeleton rather than growing a second.
out_of_scope: ServiceNow and CSV dependency support - no standard field exists and inventing a convention is a different epic (D13).
Reading the reverse direction on any connector (D14).
Any change to the forecast, to the warnings, or to how an edge is stored.
The per-Portfolio dependency field override and the ignore switch - both are slice 04.
Documentation page and screenshots - deferred to the end of the epic with the maintainer's manual verification.

quality_gates.mutation: Stryker over the files this slice wrote, kill rate >= 80%
quality_gates.review: nw-software-crafter-reviewer plus a domain reviewer before push

owed_to_manual_verification: AC-9.6's 110% wall-clock figure on a real Jira and a real Linear connection.
Real dependency links created by hand on the dogfood Jira and Linear workspaces.
The loop scenario, which cannot be dogfooded on Azure DevOps and moves here with Jira.
